items.evidence: Measured 2026-10-27: `cargo package -p bevy_emerge_core` fails before any decision is reachable — "all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging: dependency `bevy_emerge_rng` does not specify a version" (the `path` spec is dropped and crates.io is consulted). `bevy_emerge_solver` and `bevy_devshot` are also `publish = false`, so the graph has an unpublishable node in the middle. Making the workspace publishable is therefore: add a version to every intra-workspace path dependency (core->rng, core->solver, snip, anim, mapper->core/rng/solver/devshot, mcp->core), decide whether solver/devshot ship at all, then publish in dependency order rng -> solver -> core -> snip -> anim -> devshot -> mapper -> mcp. Until then the README's 'use the crates by path or git' is the only install path that works, and it is accurate. `bevy_elements` is a separate repo and already published (0.5.3, now 0.6.0).

items.title: Cmd+Z does not take away a map that was just made: there is no map_remove operation
items.evidence: map_create declares Undo::None because `take_back` applies an inverse by calling the SAME operation's commit with it, and the faithful inverse of a create is a removal — which no operation carries. map removal exists only as the chooser's Delete row (chooser.rs confirm_delete_entry, std::fs::remove_file), outside the registry. An agent can therefore make a map and not unmake it.

items.title: Notes for agents: a person marks tiles or meshes with a note, an agent works it, and the sign goes away
items.goal: A person selects one or more tiles or placed meshes and leaves a note for an agent. The note stands in the viewport as a small 3D construction sign; clicking it opens the note to read and edit. An agent lists open notes over MCP, does the work through ordinary operations and resolves the note, and its sign disappears while the change it made stays on screen. Resolved notes stay on record, so what has been worked can still be read.
acceptance: a note left on two placements and one tile is saved with the map's project and survives an editor restart
each open note shows one construction sign above its targets, and a resolved note shows none
clicking a sign opens its note; an edit to the text is saved and is one undo step
an agent over MCP lists the open notes with their targets, makes the change, resolves the note naming the operations it ran, and the sign is gone within a second while the change is on screen
resolved notes are listed with what resolved them, and an undo of the resolve brings the sign back
items.evidence: Owner's request 2026-10-28, with the focus in docs/loop/focus.md. Design defaults, so no pass has to stop for them: notes are data in the game's project beside the map they mark (one file per map, written like the map, hot-reloaded through bevy_emerge_core::live::FileWatch); a note has an id, its targets (placement ids and cells), its text, open or resolved, and on resolve the operation ids and one line of what changed; the sign is orange and white, about knee height on the map's scale, standing above the centre of its targets and never hiding them; every note change is a registered operation with undo, reachable from both the UI and MCP. The sign starts as a mesh built from Bevy primitives; a golem-made .glb replaces it only when the owner supplies one (AGENTS.md: meshes come from golem, not from this repo). A new keys::Action needs a row in the protected keys.rs census (see S3.7): ship click and button entry first and log a key as blocked rather than editing the census.
